mainTopic: Pounding and sorting food on יום טוב, and which gifts (food and clothing, including כלאים) may be sent on יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens with רבא settling two ברייתות about pounding grain in a small mortar on יום טוב: one ruling is for בבל and the other for ארץ ישראל. Then comes the story of רב פפי, who would not eat porridge at מר שמואל's house, with two possible reasons for his refusal. A new משנה follows about sorting legumes on יום טוב, with the views of בית שמאי, בית הלל and רבן גמליאל. The גמרא limits בית הלל's permission and explains how רבן גמליאל's household washed lentils. A second משנה discusses which gifts may be sent on יום טוב. The גמרא adds that gifts may not be carried in a procession of three people, and leaves רב אשי's question about three different foods as a תיקו. A third משנה allows sending clothes, even of כלאים, with the rule that anything usable on יום טוב may be sent. The גמרא then searches for a permitted use of כלאים and rejects several suggestions; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: One ruling is for us, the other for them
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles the clash between the two ברייתות by saying each one was meant for a different place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is no contradiction. This ruling is for us, and that ruling is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had two ברייתות that disagree about pounding grain in a small mortar on יום טוב, and רבא now gives his answer. He says each ברייתא is speaking to a different group of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that allows a small mortar is for the people of בבל. The ruling that forbids it is for the people of ארץ ישראל. The usual explanation is that people there had many servants, who might use a big mortar and say it was a small one, so everything was forbidden to be safe.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one ... and that one (pointing to the two sources)
For us (here, the people of בבל)
For them (here, the people of ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
This is for us, and that is for them.
phrases.notes: "Us" means the people of בבל, and "them" means the people of ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the contradiction between the ברייתות, which was raised before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources by place: each ברייתא is meant for a different community.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings for the very same case of a small mortar.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings stand. The lenient one is for בבל and the strict one is for ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב פפי refuses porridge at מר שמואל's house
steps.stepSummary: A story: on יום טוב, רב פפי was served porridge at מר שמואל's house and would not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי happened to come to the house of מר שמואל. They brought him porridge, and he did not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story connected to pounding grain on יום טוב. It sets up the questions that follow about why רב פפי refused to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Porridge is made from crushed grain. רב פפי worried that the grain had been pounded on יום טוב in a way that is not allowed. The next steps test whether his worry made sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to arrive, came by chance

phrases.english: Rav Pappi happened to come
to the house of Mar Shmuel.
They brought him porridge
and he did not eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פַּפֵּי אִקְּלַע לְבֵי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule about mortars to a real-life case of pounded grain on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפי would not eat porridge on יום טוב because he suspected the grain had been pounded in a forbidden way.

steps.title: Maybe they used a small mortar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפי's refusal: perhaps the grain was pounded in a small mortar, which is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they made it with a small mortar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רב פפי refused the food. Pounding with a small mortar is allowed, so maybe nothing wrong was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses the rule we just learned, that a small mortar is permitted. If that is how the porridge was made, there was no reason to refuse it.

keyTerms.meaning: A small mortar (bowl for pounding grain)
They made it, they did it

phrases.english: But perhaps they made it with a small mortar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the story in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's refusal to eat the porridge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small mortar is permitted, so the porridge may have been made in a permitted way.

steps.title: It was ground too finely for a small mortar
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רב פפי saw that the grain was ground very finely, which a small mortar cannot do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he saw that it was ground very finely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The porridge was so finely ground that it could not have come from a small mortar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small mortar only crushes the grain roughly. Very fine grinding means a big mortar was used, and a big mortar is forbidden, so רב פפי had good reason to refuse.

phrases.english: Because he saw that it was ground very finely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a physical sign that rules out the permitted option.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a permitted small mortar was used.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fine texture shows that a large mortar was used.

steps.title: Maybe it was made the day before
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: perhaps the grain was pounded before יום טוב, which would be fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they made it yesterday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. Even if a big mortar was used, maybe it happened the day before יום טוב, when pounding is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a big mortar is only a problem if it was done on יום טוב itself. If the grain was pounded the day before, the porridge should be fine to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, the day before (here, before יום טוב)

phrases.english: But perhaps they made it yesterday?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer in step 4 and raises a new possibility.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's refusal to eat, even after we know a large mortar was used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pounding before יום טוב is allowed, so the porridge may still be permitted.

steps.title: The grain looked freshly husked
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the grain looked fresh and shiny, which showed it had just been pounded that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he saw that its shine was freshly peeled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. The grain had the fresh look of something just crushed, so it was not prepared the day before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain that has just been pounded looks bright where the husk came off. That fresh look showed it was done on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: Because he saw that its shine was freshly peeled.
phrases.notes: The grain looked bright and fresh, a sign it had only just been pounded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a physical sign that shows when the grain was pounded.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the grain was pounded before יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fresh look proves it was pounded on יום טוב itself.

steps.title: Another reason: מר שמואל's house had careless servants
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: מר שמואל's house was different because his servants were careless about the rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: מר שמואל's house is different, because there is carelessness among the servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation for why רב פפי refused. In מר שמואל's house there were servants who were not careful, so any pounding there was suspect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not need the clues about fine grinding or fresh husks. It fits רבא's rule in step 1: where there are servants, all pounding is forbidden, because they might use a big mortar.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Carelessness, being loose about the rules

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons רב פפי refused the porridge: (1) the clues showed it was pounded in a big mortar on יום טוב; or (2) מר שמואל had careless servants, so pounding in his house was forbidden in every case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the story to רבא's rule: a strict ruling can apply to a home simply because careless servants live there.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Mar Shmuel's house is different,
because there is carelessness among the servants.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason from steps 3-6 for the story in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the refusal by the kind of house, not by the look of the food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed signs in the food to explain why רב פפי refused.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the careless servants, all pounding in that house was forbidden, so the clues are not needed.

steps.title: משנה: Sorting legumes — בית שמאי's view
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה about sorting legumes on יום טוב. בית שמאי say: pick out the food and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sorts legumes on יום טוב: בית שמאי say: He picks out food and eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about separating good legumes from the waste on יום טוב. בית שמאי give the strictest view: pick out only the food, and eat it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sorting good from bad is normally a forbidden kind of work. בית שמאי only allow picking the food itself out of the waste, and only to eat right away, not to prepare a big batch.

keyTerms.meaning: Legumes such as beans and lentils
He picks out food and eats it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read בורר אוכל ואוכל as "food and food." The first word is אוֹכֶל (food) and the second is אוֹכֵל (he eats): pick the food and eat it right away.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who sorts legumes on a Festival:
Beit Shammai say:
He picks out food and eats it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, sorting on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: only pick the food out of the waste, and eat it right away.

steps.title: בית הלל: Sort normally, but not with sorting tools
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל allow sorting in the normal way, in the lap or in household dishes, but not with tools made for sorting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: He sorts in his usual way, in his lap, with a tray or with a bowl, but not with a board, nor with a sifter, nor with a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give a more lenient view. You may sort as you normally would, but you may not use special sorting tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lap, a tray, and a bowl are ordinary ways of handling food. A board, a sifter, and a sieve are tools made for sorting, so using them looks like a regular weekday job.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
He sorts in his usual way, in his lap,
with a tray or with a bowl,
but not with a board,
nor with a sifter, nor with a sieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to בית שמאי in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: sorting in the usual way with household items is allowed, but special sorting tools are not.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: One may even rinse and skim
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל is even more lenient: you may wash the legumes in water and skim off the waste that floats up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: He may even rinse and skim off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל adds the most lenient view in the משנה. You may put the legumes in water and take off the waste that rises to the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "even" shows that he goes further than בית הלל. He allows a sorting method that uses water.

keyTerms.meaning: Skims off, draws out from the top

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views in the משנה, from strict to lenient. בית שמאי: pick out only food and eat it now. בית הלל: sort normally, but not with sorting tools. רבן גמליאל: you may even rinse in water and skim off the waste.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
He may even rinse and skim off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מֵדִיחַ וְשׁוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than בית הלל in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל: one may even wash the legumes in water and skim off the waste.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל limits בית הלל's permission to sort
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: בית הלל allow normal sorting only when there is more food than waste. When there is more waste, everyone agrees you pick out the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן גמליאל said, when did בית הלל allow this? When there is more food than waste. But when there is more waste than food, everyone agrees you take the food and leave the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that puts a limit on the leniency of בית הלל from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל allowed sorting in the normal way, which means removing the waste. רבן גמליאל explains that this only applies when most of the pile is food. When most of the pile is waste, even בית הלל agree with בית שמאי that you pick out the food.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (a phrase that limits a ruling)
Waste, the inedible part mixed with the food

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabban Gamliel said:
In what case was this said?
When the food is more than the waste,
but when the waste is more than the food,
everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאוֹכֵל וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַפְּסוֹלֶת.
phrases.english: that one takes the food and leaves the waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by limiting בית הלל's ruling from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל allow removing the waste only when the food is greater. When the waste is greater, everyone agrees you remove the food.

steps.title: Would anyone allow sorting when most of it is waste?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say 'everyone agrees' about a case that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the waste is more than the food, is there anyone who would allow it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. It seems obvious that nobody would allow removing the waste when most of the pile is waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'everyone agrees' suggest that someone might have thought otherwise. The גמרא asks who would ever allow taking out the waste when there is more waste than food. If no one would, the ברייתא's statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone? (a question that expects 'no')

phrases.english: When the waste is more than the food,
is there anyone who permits it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the need for the phrase 'everyone agrees' in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that 'everyone agrees' when the waste is greater
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No opinion would allow removing waste in that case, so stating that everyone agrees seems pointless.

steps.title: The case: less waste, but more work to remove it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means a case where the waste is smaller in amount but takes more effort to remove.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where the waste takes more work to remove but is smaller in amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'more waste' in the ברייתא means more effort, not a bigger amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is really more food than waste, so you might think בית הלל let you remove the waste. But since removing the waste takes more effort, even בית הלל say to pick out the food. Now 'everyone agrees' teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (introduces a narrow case that makes a statement useful)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'more waste' here as a bigger pile of waste. The גמרא says it means more effort, even though the waste is actually the smaller amount.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where the waste is greater in effort
but smaller in amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דִּנְפִישׁ בְּטִרְחָא וְזוּטַר בְּשִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by redefining 'greater' as greater effort.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (greater in effort, not in amount)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Waste greater than food' means a bigger amount of waste, which makes 'everyone agrees' obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the waste takes more effort but is less in amount. Even בית הלל then require picking out the food.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל allow removing the waste only when it is both smaller in amount and less work. If removing the waste is more work, everyone agrees you pick out the food.

steps.title: How רבן גמליאל's household washed lentils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's ruling from the משנה and brings a ברייתא describing his family's practice: lentils in a bucket of water, food sinking and waste floating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: one may even wash and skim off. It was taught: רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק said, this was the practice in רבן גמליאל's house: they brought a bucket full of lentils and poured water over it, and the food ended up on the bottom and the waste on top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's opinion from the משנה, then brings a ברייתא showing how his household actually did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a real example of washing and skimming. Water was poured over the lentils, the food sank, and the waste floated up where it could be skimmed off. This sets up the next question, because another ברייתא says something different.

keyTerms.meaning: Pour water over so it covers

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מֵדִיחַ וְשׁוֹלֶה.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says: one may even wash and skim off.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה we saw in step 10.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגָן שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: This was the practice of the house of Rabban Gamliel:
they would bring a bucket full of lentils
and pour water over it,
and the food ended up below
and the waste above.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגָן שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית הלל's ruling to רבן גמליאל's ruling in the משנה and illustrates it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל's household poured water over lentils so the food sank and the waste floated and could be skimmed off.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא says the food floated and the waste sank.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't the opposite taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא of step 14 with another ברייתא that says the reverse: food on top, waste on the bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות describe the same practice of washing lentils but disagree about which part floats. The גמרא needs to explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: But wasn't the opposite taught?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a contradiction against the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא saying the food sank and the waste floated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא describes the reverse, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: Dirt sinks, straw floats
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות describe different kinds of waste: dirt sinks below the lentils, straw floats above them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about dirt, and that one is about straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא talks about a different kind of waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dirt is heavy and sinks below the lentils, so the food stays on top. Straw is light and floats, so the waste ends up on top. Both ברייתות are correct, each about its own kind of waste.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about dirt,
phrases.notes: Dirt sinks, so this is the ברייתא where the waste ends up on the bottom.

phrases.english: and that one is about straw.
phrases.notes: Straw floats, so this is the ברייתא where the waste ends up on top.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּעַפְרָא, הָא בְּגִילֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases (different kinds of waste)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות describe the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: One ברייתא is about dirt, which sinks, and the other is about straw, which floats. Both are true.
steps.whatToRemember: With רבן גמליאל's washing method, where the waste ends up depends on what it is: dirt sinks and straw floats.

steps.title: What gifts may be sent on a festival
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records a מחלוקת: בית שמאי allow sending only prepared food portions on יום טוב, while בית הלל allow animals, birds, wine, oil, flour and legumes, but not grain. רבי שמעון permits grain too.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: On יום טוב you may send only portions of food. בית הלל say: You may send domestic animals, wild animals and birds, alive or slaughtered. You may send wines, oils, flours and legumes, but not grain. רבי שמעון permits grain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks which gifts a person may carry over to a friend on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי limit gifts to food that is ready to eat. בית הלל allow anything that can be used on יום טוב, like a live animal that can be slaughtered. Grain is left out because it must be ground first, and you may not grind on יום טוב. רבי שמעון disagrees and holds that grain can be used without grinding.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain, such as wheat or barley

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up the idea that runs through the whole section: a gift is allowed on יום טוב when it can be used on יום טוב.

phrases.english: MISHNA
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב אֶלָּא מָנוֹת,
phrases.english: One may send on a Festival only portions of food,
phrases.notes: מָנוֹת means food that is already prepared and ready to eat.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
One may send domestic animals, wild animals, and birds,
whether alive or slaughtered.
One may send wines, oils, flours, and legumes,
but not grain.
And Rabbi Shimon permits grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב אֶלָּא מָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the lentil discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: you may send animals, birds, wine, oil, flour and legumes, but not grain. רבי שמעון permits grain.

steps.title: Gifts may not be sent in a procession
steps.stepSummary: רב יחיאל teaches a condition: the gifts may be sent only if they are not carried in a שורה, a procession of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: רב יחיאל taught: As long as he does not send it in a procession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and adds a limit to the משנה's permission to send gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an allowed gift can become a problem if many people carry it in a line. That looks like a weekday job of moving goods, not like sending a gift for יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
As long as / on condition that
A line or procession of people carrying things

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yeḥiel teaches:
provided that he does not do it in a convoy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יְחִיאֵל: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂנּוּ בְּשׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the permission given in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gifts may be sent on יום טוב only if they are not carried in a שורה.

steps.title: How many people make a procession
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a שורה: it must have at least three people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A procession is no fewer than three people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the word שורה from the last step, so we know when the limit applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three or more people carrying, it counts as a שורה and is not allowed. With one or two people, it is not a שורה, so sending is fine.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita:
A convoy is no less
than three people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֵין שׁוּרָה פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term שורה introduced by רב יחיאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שורה is at least three people.

steps.title: Three people carrying three different foods
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: if three people each carry a different kind of food, is that still a שורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: Three men and three kinds of food, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks about a case on the edge of the definition we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three people, so it seems to be a שורה. But since each carries something different, maybe it looks like three separate gifts and not one shipment of goods.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he could not settle)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raised a dilemma:
three people and three types of food,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: תְּלָתָא גַּבְרֵי וּתְלָתָא מִינֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the three-person definition against a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a שורה need the people to carry the same kind of item, or is three people enough even with three different foods?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: no answer is found for רב אשי's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רב אשי's question stays open without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question was never settled. The case of three people carrying three kinds of food is left in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A שורה is three or more people. Whether three people with three different foods count is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of three people with three kinds of food remains unresolved.

steps.title: How grain can be used on the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with examples of how רבי שמעון means grain can be used on יום טוב without grinding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said רבי שמעון permits grain. A ברייתא taught: רבי שמעון permits grain, for example wheat to make cookies, barley to feed one's animal, and lentils to make a crushed-lentil dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי שמעון's view in the משנה and explains it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis banned grain because it seemed useless on יום טוב without grinding. The ברייתא shows that grain does have uses on יום טוב, so for רבי שמעון it counts as a usable gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of cookie made from wheat
A dish made from crushed lentils

phrases.english: The mishna taught: Rabbi Shimon permits grain.
It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon permits grain,
for example: wheat to make ludiyot from it,
barley to put before his animal,
lentils to make resisin from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר בִּתְבוּאָה, כְּגוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שורה discussion and returns to explain רבי שמעון in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, grain may be sent because it has uses on יום טוב, like cookies, animal feed, or crushed lentils.

steps.title: Sending clothes and which shoes may not be sent
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה allows sending clothes, sewn or unsewn, even with כלאים, as long as they serve the festival. But a spiked sandal and an unsewn shoe may not be sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may send clothes, sewn or unsewn, even if they contain כלאים, as long as they are for the festival's needs. But not a spiked sandal, and not an unsewn shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It moves from food gifts to gifts of clothing and shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothes may be sent, even unfinished ones or ones with כלאים, as long as they have some use for the festival. A spiked sandal cannot be worn on שבת or יום טוב, and an unsewn shoe is not usable. So those may not be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mix of wool and linen (שעטנז)
A sandal with nails in it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה lets you wear כלאים. It only allows sending such a garment when it has some use for the festival.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One may send clothes,
whether sewn or unsewn,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כִּלְאַיִם
phrases.english: and even if they contain diverse kinds,
as long as they serve the needs of the Festival.
But not a spiked sandal,
and not an unsewn shoe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשַׁלְּחִין כֵּלִים בֵּין תְּפוּרִין בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָן תְּפוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that moves from food gifts to clothing gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clothes that serve the festival may be sent. Spiked sandals and unsewn shoes may not.

steps.title: White shoes and the general rule for sending
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that a white shoe may not be sent, since it needs a craftsman to finish it. The משנה ends with a rule: anything usable on יום טוב may be sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Not even a white shoe, because it needs a craftsman. This is the rule: whatever one can use on יום טוב, one may send.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds another shoe that may not be sent, and then the משנה gives a general rule for this whole section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white shoe was not ready to wear and still needed a craftsman to color it, so it is not usable on יום טוב. The closing rule ties together the food and clothing cases: what decides it is whether the item can be used on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: The key test for sending a gift on יום טוב: can it be used on יום טוב? If yes, you may send it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule explains every case in both משניות: animals, grain, clothes and shoes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
not even a white shoe,
because it requires an artisan.
This is the principle:
anything that one may use on a Festival,
one may send it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב מְשַׁלְּחִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the clothing משנה with רבי יהודה's addition and a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything usable on יום טוב may be sent. רבי יהודה forbids a white shoe because it needs a craftsman.

steps.title: What use is a garment of כלאים on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that sewn and unsewn clothes are useful on יום טוב, but asks what use a garment of כלאים could have.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sewn clothes make sense, since you can wear them. Unsewn clothes also make sense, since you can cover yourself with them. But a garment of כלאים cannot be worn, so what is it good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. The משנה allowed sending כלאים, but the גמרא cannot see what use it has on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is that you may only send things that are usable on the festival. Wearing כלאים is forbidden, so it seems to fail that rule. The גמרא now has to find a permitted use for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (it sets up a 'but' question)
A forbidden mix, here wool and linen woven together

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Granted, sewn clothes are fit for wearing.
Unsewn clothes too are fit for covering oneself.
But כלאים, what are they fit for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from steps 23-24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to send garments of כלאים on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only things usable on יום טוב may be sent, and כלאים cannot be worn, so it seems to have no permitted use.

steps.title: Suggestion: spread it underneath yourself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that כלאים could be used as something to lie or sit on.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say the כלאים garment is useful because you can spread it underneath yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, using the words 'if you say'. This sets up the next step, where the answer is tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the Torah only forbids wearing כלאים, not lying on it. If that were true, spreading it out would be a permitted use on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

phrases.english: And if you say they are fit to spread underneath oneself,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible use to answer step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלאים has no use on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: it could be used for spreading underneath oneself. Step 27 rejects this.

steps.title: חכמים forbade lying on כלאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that חכמים forbade spreading כלאים underneath oneself, so that use fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'It shall not come upon you' means you may not wear it, but by Torah law you may spread it beneath you. However, חכמים said it is forbidden, in case a thread wraps around the person's skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion with a ברייתא. Lying on כלאים is forbidden after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, lying on כלאים would be fine. חכמים forbade it anyway, because a loose thread might touch the body, and that would be like wearing it. So spreading it out is not a permitted use.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two layers. The Torah itself allows lying on כלאים; only the rabbinic rule of חכמים forbids it.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: "It shall not come upon you"
but you may spread it beneath you.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן,
phrases.english: However, the Sages said: it is forbidden to do so,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא תִּכָּרֵךְ לוֹ נִימָא עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
phrases.english: lest a thread wrap itself around his flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of spreading כלאים underneath oneself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חכמים forbade it, in case a thread touches the skin.

steps.title: Suggestion: put something in between
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests spreading the כלאים with something separating it from the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is permitted when something separates between the person and the כלאים,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer. If there is a layer in between, the fear of a thread touching the skin goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer fixes the exact worry from the ברייתא in step 27. With a barrier in between, no thread can reach the person's body.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְסֵיק מִידֵּי בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי,
phrases.english: And if you say that something separates in between,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְסֵיק מִידֵּי בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the failed suggestion to avoid the problem raised in step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spreading כלאים underneath is forbidden because a thread may touch the skin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: with a barrier in between, it could be allowed. Step 29 rejects this.

steps.title: Even ten mattresses do not help
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the holy community of ירושלים says that even under ten mattresses, sleeping above כלאים is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, in the name of רבי, quoting the holy community of ירושלים: Even if there are ten mattresses on top of each other with כלאים underneath, it is forbidden to sleep on them, because it says, 'It shall not come upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the barrier idea with a long chain of teachers. A separation does not make it permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with ten layers in between, sleeping above כלאים is still forbidden. So putting something in between does not give כלאים a permitted use either.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi say,
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that Rabbi said in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:
phrases.notes: "רבי" on his own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עֶשֶׂר מַצָּעוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי זוֹ
phrases.english: Even ten mattresses one on top of the other
with כלאים underneath them, it is forbidden to sleep on them
(because it is said: "It shall not come upon you").
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the barrier suggestion of step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using כלאים underneath oneself with something in between.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even ten mattresses in between do not permit it.

steps.title: Suggestion: hang it as a curtain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה means a curtain of כלאים, which is hung up and not worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking about a curtain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the bedding ideas and tries a new answer: the כלאים is hung as a curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curtain is not worn or lain on, so it seems to stay away from the person's body. That would make it a permitted use on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to a curtain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed suggestions, it offers a new use for the כלאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every use of כלאים involves the body and is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a hanging curtain it would not be worn, so it could be sent.

steps.title: עולא: people warm themselves with curtains
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that a curtain can become טמא because an attendant warms himself with it, so a curtain is also used on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But עולא said: Why did they say a curtain can become טמא? Because the attendant warms himself with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the curtain answer using a statement of עולא. The גמרא's next answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, servants wrap themselves in curtains to keep warm, which is why a curtain counts as a usable item for טומאה. If so, a curtain of כלאים is also used on the body, and the curtain answer runs into the same problem.
steps.whatToRemember: Three uses for כלאים have now been tried: under oneself, under a barrier, and as a curtain. Each one runs into a source showing that the use is still forbidden: a thread might wrap around the skin, even ten mattresses do not help, and attendants warm themselves with curtains.

phrases.english: But didn't Ulla say:
For what reason did they say a curtain is impure?
Because the attendant warms himself with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the curtain answer of step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that a curtain of כלאים stays away from the body.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Attendants warm themselves with curtains, so the כלאים would be used on the body.
